**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read the nested PR metadata emitted by PR Steward**

When this compiler is fed actual `MERGE_READINESS.json` from `tools.pr_steward.classifier.build_artifacts`, the object has `pr.number` and no top-level `pr_number`/`repo` (also enforced by `schemas/pr_steward/merge_readiness.schema.json`). These required-key checks therefore raise `KeyError` before producing any `ACTION_PLAN`, so the PR Action Bridge cannot consume the steward artifacts it is meant to compile; use the emitted nested `pr` shape or update the steward artifact/schema to include the top-level fields.

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid writing absolute allowed roots into audit bundles**

If callers pass an absolute `--allowed-root` (for example `$PWD`, which is common in automation), this raw string is copied into `manifest.json` as `source_root`, exposing the host checkout path despite the bundle builder's no-host-path invariant. The bundled file paths are already relative to the root, so the manifest should store a stable redacted/relative root rather than the caller's absolute path.

This new doc references the old API surface that the same series replaced. Two stale items:

1. Lines 30-44 show `from tools.pr_action_bridge.compiler import compile` and `compile(...)`. Per TP-DMX-PR-ACTION-BRIDGE-006, the function was renamed to `compile_action_plan()` (and `compile` shadowed a Python builtin). The code examples here will not work as written and will mislead readers.

2. Line 87 of the action taxonomy table still lists `PROOF_STALE_OR_MISSING → proof-stale`. Per TP-DMX-PR-STEWARD-FRESHNESS-005 and TP-DMX-PR-STEWARD-HARDEN-010, this blocker was split into `PROOF_STALE → proof-stale` and `PROOF_MISSING → proof-missing`. The new `UNKNOWN_PR_AUTHOR → unknown-pr-author` row is also missing.

Please update both the import/call examples and the blocker taxonomy table to match the shipped code/schema in this same PR.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match actual CI triage fields when finding source items**

When the bridge compiles the `CI_TRIAGE.json` emitted by `tools.pr_steward.classifier`, check records contain fields such as `name`, `required`, `status`, `conclusion`, `head_sha`, `blocking`, and `rationale`, but no `blockers` array. This lookup therefore never matches real failed/pending/unknown checks and emits `source_item_id: null`, so the generated action plan/repair packet loses the specific failing check name despite the bridge docs describing `source_item_id` as the actionable pointer into `ci_triage`.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep unknown blocker actions schema-valid**

If `merge_readiness.blockers` contains a new or otherwise unrecognized blocker, this fail-closed branch emits `category: "unknown-blocker"`, but `schemas/pr_action_bridge/action_plan.schema.json` does not include that category in its enum. That means the compiler can produce an ACTION_PLAN that downstream schema validation rejects exactly in the compatibility case this branch is trying to handle; either add the category to the schema or map unknown blockers to an existing schema-valid supervisor category.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use actual thread disposition keys for source IDs**

When compiling real `THREAD_DISPOSITIONS.json` emitted by `tools.pr_steward.classifier`, each thread record has `is_resolved` and `thread_id`, not `resolved`/`id`. Because this lookup defaults the missing `resolved` key to `True`, an `UNRESOLVED_REVIEW_THREAD` blocker never resolves to the offending thread and the action plan emits `source_item_id: null`, removing the actionable pointer the bridge is supposed to provide.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Redact escaped absolute paths before recording rejections**

If a caller passes an absolute source outside `allowed_root`, this branch writes the raw host path into the rejected record, which is then serialized into `manifest.json`/`redactions.json`; the bundle docs promise no absolute host paths in output, so a rejected `/home/.../secret.env` can still leak checkout/user path information even though content is not read. Store a stable placeholder or root-relative-safe value for path escapes instead of `str(source)`.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match review ledger dispositions for source IDs**

The real `REVIEW_ITEM_LEDGER.json` emitted by `tools.pr_steward.classifier` stores `id`, `disposition`, `blocking`, and rationale fields, not a per-item `blockers` array. For review/comment blockers such as `REQUEST_CHANGES`, `REVIEW_ITEM_MUST_FIX`, `REVIEW_ITEM_NEEDS_SUPERVISOR`, and unknown reviewers, this lookup never finds the originating review item (and `REQUEST_CHANGES` is not in this branch at all), so ACTION_PLAN entries lose the actionable `source_item_id`. Match the ledger's `blocking`/`disposition` shape or emit blocker metadata into the ledger.

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove unsupported gh pr view field**

In live PR Steward runs this field is passed to `gh pr view --json`, but the official `gh pr view` JSON field list does not include `authorAssociation` (it includes fields such as `author`, `comments`, `reviews`, `statusCheckRollup`, etc.). GitHub CLI rejects unknown JSON fields before returning PR data, so every live harvest will fall into the `gh pr view failed` incomplete path and emit `HARVEST_INCOMPLETE` instead of classifying the PR; fetch the association through a supported field/API path or drop it from this command.
